title: Practice: Designing a Generic Cache & Repository
summary: Synthesize collections and generics into an enterprise in-memory repository: build GenericRepository<T, ID> with primary HashMap indexing, secondary TreeSet indices, functional Predicate queries, and defensive encapsulation.
learningObjectives: Design a decoupled GenericRepository<T, ID> interface supporting type-safe CRUD operations
Implement primary indexing via HashMap and secondary sorted indexing via TreeSet
Integrate functional interfaces (Predicate<T>, Function<T, ID>) for dynamic entity filtering
Return Optional<T> and immutable collection snapshots to maintain defensive encapsulation
Ensure transactional consistency across primary storage and secondary index data structures

Apply the PECS principle and modern collections to build clean, maintainable domain abstractions
Prevent internal state pollution through defensive snapshotting and immutability

activities.title: Practical Context: Library Circulation Desk & Multi-Tier Card Catalog
activities.description: How primary storage and secondary indices harmonize to provide fast, flexible data retrieval.
activities.content:
In a grand research library, books are stored in physical shelving racks identified by unique barcode IDs (`HashMap<ID, Book>`). If a patron knows the exact barcode, retrieval takes seconds.

However, patrons frequently ask: 'Show me all physics books published after 2020 in chronological order'. Wandering every shelf linearly ($O(N)$) is unacceptable. The library maintains a secondary card catalog: cards sorted chronologically (`TreeSet<Book>`) and grouped by topic (`Map<Category, Set<ID>>`). When a book is added or discarded, the librarian updates both the physical shelf and all catalog cards simultaneously.

An enterprise repository combines primary hash lookups, secondary sorted trees, and functional query predicates to deliver $O(1)$ ID lookups and logarithmic range queries while strictly shielding internal records from external tampering.

activities.title: Architecture of a Generic In-Memory Repository
activities.description: Interface contracts, dual-index synchronization, functional filtering, and defensive encapsulation.
activities.content:
### Formal Computer Science Definition
A generic repository is an architectural design pattern that abstracts data storage and retrieval mechanisms behind a strongly typed, collection-oriented interface (`Repository<T, ID>`). It encapsulates entity lifecycle mutations, maintains index invariants across multiple data structures, and provides declarative query capabilities.

### Architectural Layout

```
                                  GenericRepository<T, ID>
                                             |
                 +---------------------------+---------------------------+
                 |                                                       |
          Primary Index                                          Secondary Index
      Map<ID, T> storage                                     TreeSet<T> sortedIndex
    - O(1) findById(id)                                    - O(log N) range queries
    - O(1) save(entity)                                    - Natural / Comparator order
    - O(1) deleteById(id)                                  - Sync on every mutation
                 |
                 +--> Query Engine: findWhere(Predicate<? super T> filter)
                 +--> Encapsulation: findAll() returns List.copyOf(snapshot)
                 +--> Null Safety: findById(id) returns Optional<T>
```

### Core Design Principles

#### 1. Identity Resolution
To operate generically over any entity type `T` without forcing entities to inherit an intrusive base class, the repository accepts an identity extractor: `Function<T, ID> idExtractor`. This decouples domain entity modeling from repository persistence.

#### 2. Dual-Index Synchronization Invariant
When `save(T entity)` is invoked:
1. If an existing entity with the same ID exists, it must first be removed from all secondary indices.
2. The new entity is stored in the primary map.
3. The new entity is inserted into the secondary sorted indices.
Failure to synchronize secondary indices leads to orphaned entries and memory leaks.

#### 3. Defensive Encapsulation & Optional Returns
- **Never return raw null**: `findById(ID id)` returns `Optional<T>`. Callers explicitly handle present and absent states without null pointer risks.
- **Never expose internal collections**: `findAll()` returns `List.copyOf(storage.values())`, guaranteeing that external callers cannot mutate internal repository storage.

activities.description: Production implementation of an in-memory User repository with primary ID lookup, age sorting, and status filtering.

activities.title: Repository Architecture Evaluation
activities.description: Assess proficiency in generic repository design, index synchronization, and defensive isolation.

questions.question: When updating an entity in a dual-index repository (HashMap + TreeSet), why must the existing entity be removed from the TreeSet before inserting the updated entity?
options: Because TreeSet does not allow duplicate references under any circumstances
Because if the mutated property affects the Comparator, TreeSet will not re-sort the node in-place, corrupting binary tree invariants
Because HashMap throws an exception on overwrite
Because TreeSet only accepts immutable records
questions.explanation: TreeSet positions nodes based on Comparator comparisons at insertion time. If an object is modified while in the tree such that its sort order changes, the tree cannot detect it, corrupting tree balance and search paths. Removing before re-inserting guarantees correct re-indexing.

questions.question: Why should findById(ID id) return Optional<T> rather than returning null when an entity is not found?
options: Optional executes faster than null checks at the bytecode level
Optional forces the caller to explicitly consider the absence of data, eliminating accidental NullPointerExceptions
Optional allows multiple return values from a single method
Java 17 deprecated returning null in generic methods
questions.explanation: Optional<T> expresses intentional absence as a type contract. Callers are compelled to handle or map empty states (via ifPresent, orElse, orElseThrow), preventing silent null pointer bugs.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of returning List.copyOf(internalList) instead of internalList directly in findAll()?
options: To convert the list into a linked structure
To prevent callers from modifying internal repository storage by providing an unmodifiable defensive snapshot
To sort the list in reverse order
To enable serialization over network sockets
questions.explanation: Returning direct internal collections allows external code to call .clear() or .add(), violating encapsulation and corrupting repository state. Returning List.copyOf() ensures complete defensive isolation.

activities.title: Principal Architect System Design Interview Questions
activities.description: Staff-level design problems on repository caching, secondary indexing, and thread-safety.

questions.question: How would you design a thread-safe in-memory cache repository supporting 10,000 reads/sec and 50 writes/sec with sorted pagination?
questions.answer:
For this read-dominant workload:
1. Primary storage: ConcurrentHashMap<ID, T> provides lock-free O(1) reads for findById requests.
2. Sorted index: ReentrantReadWriteLock protects secondary index structures (or ConcurrentSkipListMap for lock-free sorted navigation).
3. Pagination & range queries: Acquire the read lock to read the ConcurrentSkipListMap or take an immutable snapshot with List.copyOf(), allowing paginated slicing without holding locks during caller consumption.
4. Write path: Acquire the write lock to update primary map and secondary skip list atomically, ensuring readers never observe partial updates.

questions.question: Why is Function<T, ID> idExtractor preferred over defining an interface like Identifiable<ID> on every domain model?
questions.answer:
Requiring entities to implement Identifiable<ID> couples the domain model directly to the persistence/repository framework (invasive design). It also makes it difficult to use the repository with third-party classes, legacy beans, or external DTOs whose code cannot be modified.

Passing Function<T, ID> adheres to the Dependency Inversion Principle: the repository is non-invasive and can persist any type T by simply supplying a method reference (e.g., User::getId or Account::accountNumber) without altering domain classes.

activities.title: Generic Repository Competency Checklist
activities.description: Assess your readiness to design robust, generic repository layers.
items: I know how to design generic interfaces with decoupled identity extractors (Function<T, ID>).
I understand why updating an entity requires removing it from secondary sorted sets prior to re-insertion.
I use Optional<T> to represent potential data absence in retrieval methods.
I protect internal repository state by returning immutable snapshots via List.copyOf().
I can filter entities dynamically using functional predicates (Predicate<? super T>).

practiceProblems.title: Basic Generic In-Memory Cache
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `SimpleCache<K, V>` providing `void put(K key, V value)`, `Optional<V> get(K key)`, `boolean contains(K key)`, and `int size()`. Keys and values cannot be null (throw `IllegalArgumentException`).

practiceProblems.title: Predicate Filter Query Executor
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `List<T> filterEntities(List<T> entities, Predicate<? super T> condition)` that evaluates `condition` on each non-null item in `entities` and returns an unmodifiable list of matching entities using `List.copyOf()`.

practiceProblems.title: Secondary Categorical Index Manager
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `SecondaryIndex<ID, Tag>` that maps a single entity `ID` to multiple categorical tags `Tag`. Implement `void addTag(ID id, Tag tag)`, `void removeTag(ID id, Tag tag)`, and `Set<ID> findByTag(Tag tag)` returning an unmodifiable Set (or empty Set if absent).

practiceProblems.title: Sorted Snapshot Repository
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `SortedRepository<T>` that accepts a `Comparator<T>` at construction. Implement `void add(T item)` and `List<T> getTop(int n)` which returns up to `n` highest-ranked items in sorted order as an immutable List snapshot.

practiceProblems.title: Keyed Identity Registry with Auto-Deduplication
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement `Registry<T, K>` with constructor `Registry(Function<T, K> keyFunction)`. Implement `void register(T item)` that overwrites existing items with the same key, and `Optional<T> lookup(K key)`.
